title: Nat.wlpo_and_markov_imply_lpo: LPO factors exactly as the weak principle plus Markov's principle
statement: Written over a Bool-valued sequence f : Nat -> Bool, which is Bishop's formulation: Hits f := exists n, f n = true ("f fires somewhere") and Misses f := forall n, f n = false ("f never fires"). LPO is forall f, Or (Hits f) (Misses f); WLPO is forall f, Or (Misses f) (Not (Misses f)); Markov's principle (MP) is forall f, Not (Misses f) -> Hits f; LLPO is forall f g, Not (And (Hits f) (Hits g)) -> Or (Misses f) (Misses g); EM is forall (P : Prop), Or P (Not P). THIS IS THE EDGE THAT MAKES THE PICTURE A MAP RATHER THAN A CHAIN. Every other implication in this family runs downhill from a stronger principle to a weaker one. This one runs back up: WLPO supplies the decision, Markov's principle supplies the witness in the branch where the sequence does not miss everywhere, and together they are exactly LPO. The consequence is a constraint on any separation result: a model of this kernel that separates LPO from WLPO must ALSO separate Markov's principle, because the two are jointly sufficient. THE PRINCIPLE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN AXIOM. It is spelled out inline in the type -- never behind a Definition -- so a reader of the rendered statement sees the whole assumption and nothing about the conclusion can be smuggled into an abbreviation. That is why axiom_footprint is empty. ADR-1601 (roadmap W0-2) decides this policy and prices it: across the ten theorems of this family the hypothesis route costs 11 binders and 14 argument positions and ZERO proof obligations. WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the principle in its hypothesis is true, false, or independent. The SEPARATIONS in the standard picture -- LPO is not constructively derivable, LLPO does not give LPO, WLPO does not give LPO, MP does not give WLPO -- are CITED here (Bishop, Constructive Analysis ch. 1) and are not proved: each needs a model of this kernel rather than a term in it, and ADR-1600 records why an internal metatheorem about this kernel is unavailable.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.wlpo_and_markov_imply_lpo : ((x0 : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.false)) (Not (((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.false))))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x2 : Not (((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x2) Bool.false))) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x3) Bool.true)))) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x3 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x2 x3) Bool.true)) (((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x2 x3) Bool.false)))))

evidence.notes: --require-declaration exits non-zero when the name is absent from every constructed prelude, and --require-kind exits non-zero when it is present with the wrong kind, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

Anchored with [[:space:]]-free literals, never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t.

evidence.supports: The statement is the one advertised, not a weaker or stronger one: the theorem is applied at GENUINELY FREE variables of the hypothesis type and the inferred conclusion is pinned against an independently rebuilt term, and a negative control in the hypothesis slot is REQUIRED TO BE REJECTED.

notes: Negative control: WLPO must NOT be accepted in Markov's slot. If it were, WLPO alone would imply LPO and the distinction between all four principles in this family would be empty. Source: crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/omniscience.rs.
